text: True or False: In set theory a function f: A → B is defined as a relation f ⊆ A × B that is total (every a ∈ A relates to some b) and single-valued (each a relates to exactly one b).
explanation: True. Functions are encoded set-theoretically as special relations — subsets of the Cartesian product A × B that are total and single-valued (functional). This reduction of functions to sets is part of encoding all of mathematics inside ZFC.
